title: Warehouse Operations Certification
description: A cumulative certification covering receiving, processing, and dispatch fundamentals across the warehouse operation. Pass to add verified Career Passport evidence for every competency this exam covers.

questions.prompt: A frozen delivery arrives and its internal temperature reads several degrees above the required threshold. What should happen before the stock is accepted into inventory?
questions.context: Frozen stock is being received at the dock, and a temperature probe check is part of the standard receiving process.

options.label: Flag the temperature breach and hold the stock before it's accepted
options.feedback: Correct -- accepting stock that has already broken cold chain just moves the problem further into the warehouse.

options.label: Accept it into inventory and make a note to check on it later
options.feedback: This lets a cold-chain breach move into stock as if nothing happened -- flag it before accepting.

questions.prompt: During a quality inspection, a batch of produce shows visible spoilage on some units but not others. What's the correct action?
questions.context: Fresh produce inspection happens after receiving, before the batch moves to storage or processing.

options.label: Segregate the affected units and hold the batch for a decision
options.feedback: Correct -- isolates the risk without discarding good stock or letting spoiled units mix in.

options.label: Pull out the visibly bad units and pass the rest through immediately
options.feedback: Spoilage often isn't fully visible yet -- the batch should be held for a proper decision, not waved through.

questions.prompt: When should a carton be checked for physical damage during receiving?
questions.context: Cartons come off the delivery truck onto the receiving conveyor in a continuous stream.

options.label: At the point of unloading, before it moves further into the flow
options.feedback: Correct -- catches damage immediately, before the carton is mixed in with other stock.

options.label: After the whole truck is unloaded, in one final pass
options.feedback: This risks damaged stock already moving deeper into the warehouse before anyone notices.

questions.prompt: An associate is about to enter the food processing area without full required PPE. What should happen?
questions.context: The processing area has a marked PPE checkpoint at its entrance.

options.label: Stop them at the entry point until PPE is complete
options.feedback: Correct -- PPE compliance has to be enforced at the point of entry, not after the fact.

options.label: Let them in and have them fix it once they're inside
options.feedback: Once inside, the hygiene risk has already occurred -- PPE must be checked at entry.

questions.prompt: A packed sack's weight reads slightly outside the acceptable tolerance on the scale. What's the correct next step?
questions.context: Sacks are weighed and sealed as part of the processing line.

options.label: Re-check the weight and correct the pack before sealing
options.feedback: Correct -- catches the shortfall or overage before the sack is sealed and shipped.

options.label: Seal it anyway since the difference is small
options.feedback: A small difference at the sack level can still add up to a real customer-facing issue -- correct it before sealing.

questions.prompt: How should a supervisor verify the quality of bags an associate has already packed?
questions.context: A supervisor oversees a team packing produce into bags on the processing line.

options.label: Spot-check completed bags directly
options.feedback: Correct -- directly checking finished output catches issues that watching the process alone would miss.

options.label: Observe the packing process from a distance
options.feedback: Watching the process doesn't catch a badly packed bag that looked fine from a distance -- check finished output directly.

questions.prompt: A refrigerated vehicle has just backed into the frozen dock bay. When should its internal temperature be verified relative to loading?
questions.context: Frozen stock is staged at the dock, ready to be loaded once the vehicle is ready.

options.label: Before any crates are loaded
options.feedback: Correct -- loading into a vehicle that hasn't reached temperature defeats the cold chain before the trip starts.

options.label: Partway through loading, once a few crates are already in
options.feedback: By then some stock has already gone into a vehicle that wasn't ready -- verify before loading starts.

questions.prompt: When should a vehicle's tamper-evident security seal be applied and confirmed?
questions.context: A refrigerated vehicle has just finished loading at the dispatch dock.

options.label: Right after loading finishes, before the vehicle leaves
options.feedback: Correct -- closes the tamper-evidence gap before the vehicle ever moves.

options.label: Whenever convenient before the next trip
options.feedback: This leaves the vehicle unsealed and unverified in the meantime -- seal it right after loading.

questions.prompt: When should a driver's route assignment be confirmed against the assignment board?
questions.context: Drivers gather near their staged vehicles before departure.

options.label: Before the driver departs with the vehicle
options.feedback: Correct -- catches a mix-up while it's still easy to fix.

options.label: After departure, if a stop seems wrong
options.feedback: By then the driver is already on the wrong route -- confirm before departure instead.

questions.prompt: An associate notices an item appears to be missing from an order on the sortation line. What should happen?
questions.context: Orders move along a sortation line where contents are checked against labels.

options.label: Flag the order and escalate it before it continues
options.feedback: Correct -- catches the issue before it becomes a customer-facing problem.

options.label: Let it continue and note it for later
options.feedback: This lets an incomplete order reach the customer -- flag and escalate immediately instead.

questions.prompt: When should product temperature be verified during a chilled delivery to a restaurant?
questions.context: A delivery associate has arrived at a restaurant with chilled stock.

options.label: At the point of handover, before the restaurant accepts it
options.feedback: Correct -- confirms the cold chain held all the way to the customer.

options.label: Skip it -- the vehicle was refrigerated, so it should be fine
options.feedback: A refrigerated vehicle doesn't guarantee the product itself held temperature -- always verify at handover.

questions.prompt: A restaurant raises a shortage claim while a delivery is being unloaded. How should the delivery associate respond?
questions.context: Both the delivery associate and the restaurant carry handheld devices with order records.

options.label: Check the device record against what was actually delivered
options.feedback: Correct -- settles the dispute with the actual record instead of guesswork.

options.label: Accept the customer's claim without checking
options.feedback: This risks incorrect adjustments -- always verify against the device record first.
